newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Forbes hits new yr high on Nelson Hurst bid.
newsitem.headline: Forbes hits new yr high on Nelson Hurst bid.

text.p: Shares in South African insurance firm Forbes Group Ltd surged on Wednesday after the company announced it had made a cash offer to increase its stake in British marine insurance firm Neslon Hurst Plc, dealers said.
By about 0758 GMT the Forbes stock was up 60 cents at 10.10 rand after earlier surging to a new year high of 10.50 rand.
Volumes were fair with 85,300 shares valued at around 824,000 rand exchanging hands.
"They're (shares) up on this announcement that (the company) has now made a cash offer for Nelson Hurst. It looks like guys are taking this as a positive move," one dealer said.
The dealer said that because the stock had peaked immediately after the start of trade it would likely cool off during the course of day.
"They have started higher up and I think the share will now just drift off," he said.
Nelson Hurst announced earlier on Wednesday that the Forbes Group had made a recommended 84.5 million sterling cash offer for it through FG (UK) Ltd, a wholly-owned firm.
It said in a statement that the offer is for 185 pence for each Nelson Hurst share.
Nelson Hurst said the price represented a premium of 43 percent to Tuesday's closing market price of 129.5 pence.
Nelson Hurst directors have irrevocably undertaken to accept the offer in respect of 5.1 million shares, around 11.17 percent of the issued share capital.
Forbes, a leading provider of risk management, insurance and employee benefits related services in South Africa, currently owns 9.94 percent of Nelson Hurst.
